# BLOCK — PR 277, round 1

Reviewed head `f9d2bc77871f3d7cee6418d6d18c86c26d5e40f4` against

## R277-1 — P2: a local timeout is not positive receive-path readiness

`.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:1751-1759`

The new catch branch reports `connection-ready` and clears `failureEpisode`
when the client times out without receiving response headers. That does not
establish that the daemon accepted the claim: `#requestEnvelope:760-762`
classifies any unanswered inbox fetch reaching its own deadline this way.
A delayed refusal or a request stalled before admission takes the same branch
as a healthy idle long poll.

Independent regression: the fixture refuses the first claim with 401,
successfully re-registers, and delays the next 401 until after the client
deadline. This head reports reconnected despite no accepted claim. The test
fails with ready count 1 instead of 0, and passes against the base's store.mjs.
Require positive receive-path evidence before ending the outage; don't use
silence at a client deadline as an acknowledgement.

The deviation from clearing on re-registration/heartbeat correctly avoids
the reported flap when registration succeeds but claims fail; it does not
make the replacement timeout signal sound. Successful empty/message claims
still end the episode normally. A returned 4xx, a response-body stall, a
foreign timeout, or external cancellation does not take this new branch;
the failure is specifically a refusal not received before the local timer.

## R277-2 — P2: the D1 edge history is lost on daemon restart

`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:366` and `:462-465`

`native_lapsed` is rebuilt empty, rather than restored or reconciled with the
last durable edge. For a seat already told lapsed, a daemon restart followed
by no heartbeat emits another lapsed event after boot grace. If its heartbeat
arrives during grace instead, the set's remove returns false, so the durable
pre-restart lapse gets no matching renewal. This violates the packet's
cross-restart edge requirement; neither outcome is covered by the new
single-service-lifetime test.

Independent SQLite regression: heartbeat, advance 61 seconds, reconcile
twice, destroy the services, reopen the same store, advance 61 seconds, and
reconcile twice. The durable edge sequence is `lapsed`, `lapsed` (the second
has `renewed_at:null`), not one outstanding lapse; assertion 2 versus 1 fails.

Keep the told state consistent with durable edges across restart, without
emitting a renewal for a seat with no preceding lapse. The existing retain
does prune tombstoned/non-native seats during ordinary reconciliation.

## R277-3 — P2: saturation hides unrelated seats' first refusals

`crates/daemon/src/registration/refusals.rs:44`

Once 512 distinct unexpired `(seat, code)` pairs are present, the vacant-entry
capacity branch returns false for every other pair. A different seat's first
refusal therefore produces neither its event nor its log line, potentially
for almost ten minutes, solely because other seats filled the window.
The existing capacity test expects that suppression. Eight static outcome
codes reach the window, so the keys need not come from malformed claimants
to exhaust its capacity.

Preserve bounded memory and non-blocking registration, but don't let other
seats consume all first-refusal visibility. Make the chosen overflow behavior
explicit and cover a different seat's first refusal at capacity. The window
is a **noise brake**, not registration policy: removing it only tells more.

The scoped security review found no new secrets/credential-text disclosure or
log injection. The D2 issue above is a requested visibility/correctness
invariant, not a new account trust-boundary vulnerability. Codes and attempt
paths come from static enums. The digest escapes the whole seat argument
with `shell_word` and adds advice only; no restart is automatically run.

The three relaxed tests still exclude any added non-refusal events. Existing
independent roster/queue, original-row, and refused-probe absence assertions
are retained. Invalid-evidence/no-registry behavior was not loosened by the
changed event assertions. No warning/model_http 401 trigger was added.

## Cost

No new process launch, timer or poll. The banner adds no request; D1 rides
existing receiver reconciliation/heartbeat and writes only on edges; D2 scans
at most 512 in-memory pairs per refusal and adds no registry lookup. D1 adds
another live-seat retain scan alongside the existing lease pruning. The
restart command remains text.

Live deployed-fleet counters rose from 615 to 619 during the observation
interval, all four launches attributed to registration host verification.
`just spawn-rate --seconds 20` reported 367.9 machine-wide launches/s and no
observed daemon-child launches. These are background fleet receipts, not an
undeployed-PR before/after comparison.
